newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
THE 100M STG TUBE LINE TO NOWHERE

A brand new 100 million stg signalling system installed on London Underground's Central Line broke down during yesterday's rush hour, causing an important section of the line to be out of action. Although the line was working again this morning, there is a possibility of further problems with the new signalling system to come.
US PUTS SQUEEZE ON MONEY LAUNDERING

Efforts by the US to eradicate money laundering could lead European institutions to unwittingly fall foul of American law, according to City lawyer Rowan Bosworth-Davies of Titmuss Sainer Dechert. He says that the American drive means that British institutions will have to conform to global standards if they want to be global players. Last month three foreign bankers were convicted and imprisoned in New York because the proceeds of a fraud that took place in Venezuela were moved via the New York banking system, thus bringing them under US jurisdiction.
BEARS PUSH THE POUND INTO REVERSE GEAR
Sterling continued to fall overnight, losing half a pfenning against the Deutschmark, in reaction to weak economic figures yesterday and a growing expectation that Emu's start date will be delayed.
THE BOMB TICKING IN THE BOARDROOMS

Research by Manifest Voting Agency, which monitors quoted companies in the interests of institutional shareholders, found that a total of 13 directors were aged 80 or over at the time of writing, while 12 were sitting on the boards of six or more quoted companies. Despite Sir Adrian Cadbury's report recommendation that no one should be both chief executive and chairman of a public company, the research found 103 people filling both roles, including two in the FT-SE 100 - Sir Ian Prosser at Bass and Sir Brian Moffat at British Steel.
